$comment: Which migrations reconstruct a database, and which only repair this one.
The chain contains two kinds of migration. Schema and deterministic
configuration must rebuild from this repository into an empty database —
that is the disaster-recovery property. Historical data repairs correct
specific real records on MAIN; replaying them into an empty database is
meaningless, and the assertions that make them trustworthy there would
have to be gutted to make them pass here.
So they are listed, not weakened. Everything absent from this file is
deterministic and MUST replay from empty. A new migration is deterministic
by default; adding it here is a deliberate act.
owns_durable_schema means the migration also creates structure or
configuration the finished CRM needs. Such a migration CANNOT simply be
skipped: the structure has to be reconstructible on its own first, or the
rebuilt database silently lacks it. Those are flagged unresolved below.
Eight of these once owned durable structure as well. It was extracted to
20260918155000 (columns, CHECKs, the payment-intent index, four functions,
two guard triggers, the reconcile-stripe schedule), 20260919020000
(record_deal_outcome_event, which a deterministic migration would
otherwise overwrite) and 20260918275000 (the commercial-total provenance
column and its CHECK). Their data repairs and assertions are unchanged.
Three entries were added only after a clean-room replay refused them:
by inspection and are in fact named-client repairs. Static review missed
them because the old audit could only ask whether a declared MAIN-only
migration was safe to skip, never whether an undeclared one should have
been listed. reviewedDeterministic() in replayBoundary.mjs now asks the
second question too.
Facts about the ENVIRONMENT that no migration can create for itself.
A rebuilt database needs these in place before the chain is replayed,
or migrations that schedule work fail closed — correctly, since an
unauthenticated scheduled call is worse than a missing one.
Discovered by replaying into an empty project, not assumed.
